subject: Onboarding evidence ask and PO deferment steps
messages:
From: Ellie Ramos <ellie@blueharbor.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor onboarding — pilot contract and PO timing

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — we are excited to kick off the 6-week pilot with Redwood. One operational hitch on our side: our procurement team requires a purchase order for any vendor that charges against our central ledger, and their cycle will not issue a PO until the SOW is fully executed. We are trying to avoid delaying the technical kickoff.

Question: would Redwood accept a short-term deferment (30–60 days) on PO issuance if we provide an executed SOW and a single consolidated invoice at the end of the pilot? Procurement said they can sign a conditional confirmation email and provide a remittance contact, but they need an onboarding checklist and any risk-evidence (SOC2, data residency notes) to move fast.

I attached the internal onboarding checklist they asked to share (attachment: BH_Onboard_Checklist.pdf) — let us know what you need from Redwood to make the deferment acceptable.

Best,
Ellie Ramos
Program Manager, Strategic Partnerships
BlueHarbor Labs

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — pilot contract and PO timing

Hi Ellie — thanks for the clear note and the checklist. Short answer: yes, we can often accommodate a temporary PO deferment for pilots if we have a clear, timeboxed fallback and the right procurement evidence.

What we need from your side to move this through our finance and legal reviews: 
- Executed SOW (even a slim one-page statement is fine) — we can work from your template.
- Confirmation email from your procurement (procure@blueharbor.ai) that they will issue a PO within 60 days and who the remittance/approver is.
- SOC2 or equivalent evidence (if available) and the completed onboarding checklist you sent.

Our proposed conditional approach: 
1) We accept a 60-day PO deferment for the pilot period, with Redwood issuing invoices monthly and pausing after 60 days if the PO has still not been received (we will not pursue collections during the deferment window unless there is nonpayment after PO issuance).
2) If PO is not provided within 60 days, finance requires either (a) a virtual card payment for outstanding invoices or (b) escalation to procurement for a short-term PO exception that may require approval from Hanna (Finance) and Commercial Ops.
3) We need an internal sign-off from our finance owner (David) before we finalize.

I'll attach a draft of the SOW we suggest (SOW-Redwood-v1.docx) and a short evidence checklist for our side. Can you confirm the procurement contact who will send the conditional confirmation? If you can get that today, I will loop David for quick sign-off.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0127

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — pilot contract and PO timing

Small follow-up from ops: if we go the 60-day deferment route, I recommend we: 
- Record a single-line clause in the SOW: "PO to follow within 60 days; in absence of PO, invoices become payable via virtual card or subject to exception approval."
- Ask for a named procurement approver and an Escalation SLA (e.g., procurement will respond to PO requests within 7 business days once initiated).
- Take a quick risk score: revenue < $25k for this pilot would make auto-exception easier; if it's > $25k we should require an interim payment method.

Also +1 on getting SOC2 or similar — if BlueHarbor can share the link, we can mark low-risk and expedite.

Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Ops, Redwood

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — pilot contract and PO timing

Ellie — thanks for sending the checklist. BlueHarbor's proposed path is acceptable under these conditions: 

1) We receive the executed SOW (signed by BlueHarbor) before the technical kickoff.
2) BlueHarbor procurement sends the conditional confirmation email to procure@redwood.ai confirming a PO will be issued within 60 days and naming the remittance contact.
3) BlueHarbor provides either a SOC2 report link or evidence of an equivalent control (screenshot or attestation).

Operational commitments from Redwood: we will start work on the technical kickoff (sandbox access and onboarding call) once items 1–3 are in place. We will invoice monthly; if PO is not received within 60 days we will notify and request payment via virtual card or follow the exception escalation.

Next steps: 
- Ellie, please share the SOW signed copy and procurement confirmation.
- Hannah, Marissa: I'll create a short Finance approval note (OPS-412) to document the deferment and record the risk score.

If BlueHarbor is comfortable, let's schedule a 20-minute alignment call tomorrow at 10:00 PT to confirm names and timelines.

Best,
David
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
Phone: (650) 555-0199
